Old_Answer: Every time they come back around, you remain indifferent, say no and stop allowing them back in. You stop putting your life on hold for them, no longer make yourself easily accessible/available, go no contact and never reach out to them again. This gets very easy and is even a decision that comes naturally to you when you have self-worth and self-respect. Because nobody who truly loves and respects themselves will tolerate dynamics of unrequited love and wont chase after or pursue a relationship with someone emotionally unavailable who doesn’t want them, who, through their actions and behaviors, has consistently revealed that they don’t have their best interest at heart.

Understand that every time you allow them back into your life, you’re reopening old wounds and prolonging your healing process. It’s crucial to prioritize your emotional well-being and practice self-love. Engage in activities that bring you joy and fulfillment, and surround yourself with supportive friends and family who uplift you. Reflect on the reasons why this person is not a good match for you; often, it’s easier to romanticize the past than to confront the reality of the relationship. Journaling can be a powerful tool for processing your feelings and gaining clarity. Additionally, consider implementing a no-contact rule; this will help you break the cycle of hope and disappointment. Remember, healing takes time, and it’s okay to grieve the relationship you wished you had. Focus on rediscovering your identity outside of this connection, and allow yourself to envision a future where you attract healthier, more fulfilling relationships. Ultimately, you deserve someone who values you and your feelings, not someone who keeps breaking your heart.

However, this doesn’t necessarily mean they want to reconcile. They could be seeking validation, attention, or simply testing the waters to see how you respond. It’s crucial to recognize that mixed signals often stem from their internal conflict rather than a clear desire to get back together. If they’re oscillating between warmth and coldness, it’s a sign that they haven’t fully committed to moving on, which can be confusing for you. But remember, this indecisiveness can be detrimental to your healing process. Instead of getting caught up in their emotional rollercoaster, focus on your own well-being. Establishing boundaries and maintaining no contact can help you regain clarity and prevent further emotional turmoil. Ultimately, mixed signals are a reflection of their unresolved feelings, not a roadmap for your future. Prioritize your healing and self-discovery, and don’t let their ambiguity dictate your emotional state. You deserve clarity and stability, and the best way to achieve that is by stepping back and allowing both yourself and your ex the space to figure things out independently.
